question: For positive integers \(m\) and \(n\) such that \(m + 10 \lt n + 1,\) both the mean and the median of the set \(\{m, m + 4, m + 10,\) \(n + 1,\) \(n + 2,\) \(2n\}\) are equal to \(n.\) What is \(m + n?\)
solution:
The ordering lets us identify the middle two numbers. Since \(m\ge1\) and \(m+10<n+1\), we have \(n\ge11\), so \(n+2<2n\). Therefore all six numbers are listed in increasing order.

For six numbers, the median is the average of the third and fourth. Thus
\[
\frac{(m+10)+(n+1)}{2}=n,
\]
which gives \(m+n+11=2n\), or \(m=n-11\).

Substitute this into the condition that the mean is \(n\):
\[
\frac{(n-11)+(n-7)+(n-1)+(n+1)+(n+2)+2n}{6}=n.
\]
Combining terms gives
\[
7n-16=6n,
\qquad n=16.
\]
Then \(m=16-11=5\), which satisfies the required inequality \(15<17\). Hence
\[
m+n=5+16=\boxed{21},
\]
choice \(\text{B}\).
